chunks.title: Profile and overview
chunks.text: Jayce Nhan Parabellum (he/him) is an AI Software Engineer based in Denver, Colorado. Jayce builds LLM applications that run on local or managed models, with agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over vector databases, Docker packaging, and CI evaluation gates that stop bad releases. Jayce is a United States Armed Forces veteran (U.S. Marine Corps, D.C. Air National Guard, and U.S. Air Force Reserve) and is Top Secret clearance eligible.

chunks.title: Profile and overview
chunks.text: Since August 2026 Jayce has been an AI Software Engineer at Teos Technology, LLC (remote, Colorado Springs, CO), building HIPAA-aligned LLM clinical documentation and triage services for skilled nursing facilities.

chunks.title: Profile and overview
chunks.text: Jayce spent six years in the U.S. Marine Corps (2008-2014) as a metal worker who made Sergeant, then served as an aerospace propulsion (jet engine) mechanic in the D.C. Air National Guard on the C-40 (2014-2022) and the U.S. Air Force Reserve on the C-5M Galaxy (2021-2024), reaching Staff Sergeant and a 7-level. In parallel Jayce moved into federal IT: network and systems work for CACI at the Pentagon and Phacil at Marine Corps Recruiting Command (2017-2019), then nearly six years at Perspecta/Peraton (December 2019 - August 2025), ending as Cloud Systems Architect, Lead Associate on the NBIS personnel-vetting platform in AWS GovCloud. In 2026 Jayce completed the Gauntlet AI Fellowship (Cohort 4) and joined Teos Technology as an AI Software Engineer. Jayce is pursuing an M.S. in Computer Science (Artificial Intelligence) at CU Boulder, expected June 2028.

chunks.title: Profile and overview
chunks.text: Jayce's engineering approach comes from the flight line, where a 7-level signs for every job against technical data before an aircraft flies: nothing leaves the shop without a sign-off. Jayce builds AI systems the same way, measured, traceable and honest about what they don't know, around three principles. Ground every answer: retrieval over the real source material (regulations, protocols, patient records) with citations required, and the system says so when the sources don't cover a question instead of guessing; the TTB label verification tool and the clinical co-pilot work this way. Gate every release: versioned prompts, golden datasets, regression replay and canary rollouts with automatic rollback, so a change ships when the evals say so, not when the demo looks good; this is the release process Jayce uses at Teos. Secure by default: PHI de-identified at ingest, tenant-scoped retrieval, audit logs, authentication on every endpoint and STIG-hardened hosts, a habit from six years of NIST and RMF work on federal cloud systems.

chunks.title: Profile and overview
chunks.text: Jayce is interested in AI engineer, applied AI, and AI platform roles, especially ones that combine LLM applications with secure cloud infrastructure, regulated environments (healthcare, government, finance), and production evaluation. Jayce also has a strong software engineering and cloud solutions architecture background, which suits solutions architect and cloud architecture roles. Jayce is open to three kinds of work: freelance or contract projects, full-time corporate roles, and consulting engagements. For specifics about availability, compensation, or relocation, contact Jayce directly.

chunks.title: Gauntlet AI Fellowship - AI Engineer, Challenger, Cohort 4 (Apr - Aug 2026)
chunks.text: Stack: Python, FastAPI, LangGraph, Claude and Ollama, Postgres, Docker, GitHub Actions. Built and deployed an AI compliance tool that checks alcohol beverage labels against 27 CFR (TTB regulations) and returns PASS/FLAG verdicts. Scored 100% correct decisions on a 24-case eval set with a 211 ms worst-case response, and hands unreadable labels to a human reviewer instead of guessing. The LangGraph assistant runs on Claude in the cloud or Ollama locally, with human confirmation on every write and a hash-chained audit log in Postgres. It uses citation-grounded RAG over 27 CFR with BM25 and BGE embeddings combined by reciprocal rank fusion, and refuses when the regulations don't cover the question. Every release was gated on 446 automated tests, a RAG eval and a replayed agent-behavior eval in GitHub Actions. Jayce fixed 21 CVEs and added upload limits and security headers before launch. Code: github.com/jayceparabellum/TTB_AI_Label_Verification_Tool

chunks.title: About this AI assistant
chunks.text: This site's assistant is a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that Jayce built to showcase his AI engineering. The knowledge base is a set of curated markdown files about Jayce's career, chunked by section. For each question, a Cloudflare Worker (1) rewrites follow-up questions into standalone search queries with Llama 3.1 8B, (2) runs hybrid retrieval: BM25 keyword search plus dense vector search with BGE embeddings on Cloudflare Workers AI, (3) merges both rankings with reciprocal rank fusion, (4) reranks the candidates with a BGE cross-encoder reranker, and (5) streams a grounded answer from Meta's Llama 3.3 70B model, running on Cloudflare Workers AI, that cites its sources and declines when the knowledge base doesn't cover the question. Rate limiting, input limits, an origin allowlist, prompt-injection rules and signed conversation history protect the endpoint, and everything runs on Cloudflare's free tier with no third-party API keys. The code is public in the site's GitHub repository under chat-worker/.

chunks.title: About this AI assistant

It will not share private details such as phone number, home address, or credential numbers, it won't speculate about salary expectations, and it doesn't make up facts that aren't in its sources.
